title: Nasruddin Tale 196: The Man Who Would Not Give
summary: A wealthy miser fell into a deep river and was drowning. The villagers ran along the bank, shouting: "Give us your hand! Give us your hand!"...
full_text:
A wealthy miser fell into a deep river and was drowning. The villagers ran along the bank, shouting: "Give us your hand! Give us your hand!"

The miser refused to stretch out his hand, for in his entire life he had never given anything to anyone.

Nasruddin leaned over the bank and shouted: "Take my hand! Take my hand!"

The miser immediately grabbed Nasruddin's hand and was pulled to safety.

Nasruddin explained: "He has never learned the word 'give,' but he understands the word 'take' perfectly!"
moral: To reach a miser, speak the language of receiving rather than giving.
